clue.text: Month's work's involved in unknown film

indicators.note: the work is involved, wrapped up, within the letters for the month's

parts.note: OCT is the calendar abbreviation for October, plus the S of the possessive
an opus is a musical or literary work; the 's is just 'is'
algebra's unknowns are x, y and z

explanation.surface: A mystery film somehow involves a month's worth of work.
explanation.walkthrough: The month's S stays on the end, so the work sits between OCT and S before the unknown is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Octopussy is a 1983 James Bond movie starring Roger Moore.

clue.text: Confess to have finished

parts.note: to own something is to have it
time is up when it is finished

explanation.surface: Admitting that one has finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to admit a fault, an idiom for confessing.

clue.text: You do office jobs the old-fashioned way? Rather a blow

definitions.text: You do office jobs the old-fashioned way?
definitions.meaning: first meaning: thou ..., the archaic second-person form of temp, to do temporary office work
second meaning: a storm, rather more than a mere blow of wind

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned office temping comes as a rather nasty blow.
explanation.walkthrough: Old English verb forms added -est for thou, so thou temp becomes thou tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent windstorm, a gale stronger than an ordinary blow.

clue.text: Traveller turns up — sometime later an artiste

indicators.note: the word for sometime comes after
in a down answer, turning up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative
sometime as an adjective means former, onetime

explanation.surface: A traveller turns up some time later, an artiste on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sometime' reads as 'at a later point' but is the adjective meaning onetime.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer is an entertainer, the same as an artiste on stage.

clue.text: Senior officials, one tight-lipped about April 1 birthday?

parts.note: someone who keeps quiet about a matter keeps it secret
someone born on April 1 has the star sign Aries

explanation.surface: Senior officials include one who won't reveal a birthday on April Fools' Day.
explanation.walkthrough: Read together, someone tight-lipped about an April 1 birthday is a secret Aries.
explanation.definitionFit: Secretaries of state are senior government ministers, the top officials in a department.

clue.text: Deviate from route northwards

indicators.note: in a down answer, going north means reading upwards

parts.note: a way is a route

explanation.surface: Straying off a course heading north.
explanation.definitionFit: To yaw is for a ship or aircraft to swing off its course.

clue.text: Subject that's closed, still?

parts.note: a door that is 'to' is pushed shut
a still is a photograph, a pic

explanation.surface: Is a matter that is settled and finished still up for discussion?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as an adverb but is the noun for a single photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the subject of a talk or discussion.

clue.text: One having shot janitor finally enters bank

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the word for bank

parts.note: a tier is a row or bank of seats

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: the word whose last letter is used

explanation.surface: A janitor who has been shot finally walks into a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests gunfire in a bank raid; here it means an attempt, a go.
explanation.definitionFit: A trier is someone who makes an attempt, who has a shot at something.

clue.text: Bang on about one's spruce clothes (endlessly)

indicators.note: to clothe is to cover, so the shortened word wraps around the rest
the word for spruce loses its last letter

parts.note: to spruce up is to preen
c, circa, means about
one is I, and 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone banging on about how spruce their clothes are, endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bang on' looks like 'go on and on' but means exactly right. 'Clothes' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Bang on is British slang for exactly correct, which is what precise means.

clue.text: Getting by with dated tool

parts.note: coping means managing, getting by
if you saw someone you dated them, went out with them

explanation.surface: Getting by with an old-fashioned tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dated' looks like 'old-fashioned' but is the verb to go out with.
explanation.definitionFit: A coping saw is a small bow saw for cutting curves in wood.

clue.text: Senseless not to finish, chap figured?

indicators.note: the word for senseless is not allowed its final letter

parts.note: numb means without feeling
Eric is any man's name, a crossword chap

explanation.surface: Someone foolish who never finishes things is supposedly a chap who has worked it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figured' looks like a verb, but here it is the adjective, expressed in figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Numeric means expressed as numbers, so something figured in digits.

clue.text: This report from auditor's going all the way to the top?

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so we want what a hearer would take the phrase to be

parts.words: going all the way to the top
parts.note: right up, as in climbing right up to the summit

explanation.surface: An auditor's report is escalated all the way to the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' reads as an accountant checking books, but it means a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: A write-up is a written account or review, a report on something.

clue.text: One used to spell in Greece: West Ham's star Italian?

parts.words: One used to spell in Greece
parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, used in spelling there

indicators.note: West Ham is in East London, where Cockneys drop their aitches

parts.note: the star of a story is its hero

explanation.surface: A West Ham football star turns out to be an Italian who could cast spells in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: West Ham is an East London football club; Cockney speech there drops the initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: Piero is an Italian man's name, as in the painter Piero della Francesca.

clue.text: Close to nine, dawn raid put off from earlier time

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the word whose final letter is used

indicators.note: dawn raid is put off, thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to be rearranged
taken as written, part of the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A police dawn raid at nearly nine is postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put off' looks like postponement in the raid scene; it signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwardian describes the era of King Edward VII, 1901 to 1910, an earlier period.

clue.text: Worked with energy: appropriate for the type of job

parts.note: something that worked was a hit
to collar something is to seize, appropriate it

explanation.surface: Working energetically at the right sort of job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective in the surface; in the wordplay it is the verb to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: White-collar work is office work, describing a kind of employment.

clue.text: Court oddly leading to nick

indicators.note: take the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth

parts.note: the word whose letters are picked

explanation.surface: An odd court case ends with someone in the nick, or prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick is British slang for prison, which the surface leans on; here it means a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A nick is a small incision, synonym for a slight wound.

clue.text: One struggling to go through: nearly all at stake

parts.note: to comb an area is to go through it thoroughly
taken as written

indicators.note: all of the phrase at stake except its last letter

parts.note: the ante is the stake in poker

explanation.surface: Someone straining to get through when nearly everything is at stake.
explanation.definitionFit: A combatant is a fighter, someone engaged in a struggle.

clue.text: Empty fireplaces getting in the way

indicators.note: the fireplaces get inside the word for the way

parts.note: means is a way or method of doing something
an ingle is a hearth or fireside

explanation.surface: Empty fireplaces are obstructing someone's path through the room.
explanation.walkthrough: Ingle, an old word for fireside, survives in inglenook.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaningless and empty both describe words or gestures that lack any substance.

clue.text: Development stage not normally launched into

indicators.note: the word stage is not in its normal order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the word into is launched, sent flying, into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A stage of development that is not normally entered upon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Launched into' looks like a phrase meaning started; the two words split up, one the signal and one the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestation is the development of an embryo in the womb, or of an idea over time.

clue.text: Being near failure involves I hesitate to say punishment

definitions.note: a noun phrase: near here means stingy, so being near is a state

indicators.note: the word for failure wraps around the following pieces

parts.note: a miss is a failed attempt
er is the sound of hesitation
lines are a school punishment, writing a sentence over and over

explanation.surface: Someone close to failing is hesitant to name the punishment due.
explanation.walkthrough: Near is old British usage for mean with money, which the surface hides as 'close'.
explanation.definitionFit: Miserliness is stinginess, and near is a dated word for tight-fisted.

clue.text: My job is getting harder!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the setter's job is ... the crossword
second meaning: ..., as concrete or jelly firms up

explanation.walkthrough: The setter speaks in the first person, so the complaint that the job is getting harder hides a word for both.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting is both composing a puzzle and the process of becoming solid.

clue.text: Gym with place to sit

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym

explanation.surface: A gym that comes with somewhere to sit down.
explanation.definitionFit: A pew is a bench seat in a church.

clue.text: Scoff at local boxer devouring book with massage

indicators.note: the boxer devours, takes inside, the letter for book

parts.note: a pug is a pugilist, a boxer; also a dog breed
a rub is a massage

explanation.surface: A boxer wolfing down a book alongside a massage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' looks like 'jeer at', but it is British slang for food. A local is a neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Pub grub is food served in a pub, which is the scoff at your local.

clue.text: Hors d'oeuvres for now, it's implied? There's nothing to follow

indicators.note: nothing comes after the first piece, at the end

parts.note: being for the present suggests being against the past, anti-past
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A cheeky waiter serves starters now, with nothing to come after them.
explanation.walkthrough: Favouring the present is read as opposing the past; the question mark flags that leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian starter course of cured meats and olives, served before the meal.

clue.text: Tuck into apple: a treat!

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the letters of the next words

parts.note: the answer runs across these words, from the end of apple into treat

explanation.surface: Tuck into an apple, what a treat!
explanation.walkthrough: Tuck looks like the verb to eat heartily, a British sense, but it is a fold in fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold or tuck in cloth, sewn to hold its shape.

clue.text: Superior rating given to second rate books

parts.note: a rating is an ordinary sailor, an AB or able seaman
B grade is second rate
OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of books

explanation.surface: A superior rating goes to second-rate books, a puzzling review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior' looks like an adjective about the rating, but it is the head of a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbot is the superior, the head, of an abbey of monks.

clue.text: At least three Queen's companions in Siberian city

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, and toms are male cats
a king, another companion of a queen in a pack of cards, makes at least three with the toms

explanation.surface: At least three companions of the Queen visit a Siberian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen is read as a female cat whose mates are toms, plus K for king.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomsk is a major university city in western Siberia, Russia.

clue.text: An American serving Dutch painter with dexterity

parts.note: taken as the single letter a
a GI is an American soldier on service
Sir Peter Lely was a Dutch-born portrait painter at the English court

explanation.surface: An American waiter serves a Dutch painter with deft skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serving' suggests waiting at table, but it means serving in the army.
explanation.definitionFit: Agilely means nimbly, moving with quickness and skill.

clue.text: Studies after missing start of course

indicators.note: the word for studies is used after losing its first letter

parts.note: to eye something is to study it

explanation.surface: Someone's studies have missed the start of the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' looks like part of the study course; it is the answer's meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Of course is an emphatic yes, agreeing that something is certain.

clue.text: Moor and lake to west, by border county

indicators.note: in an across answer west is leftwards, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to moor a boat is to tie it up
L for lake on maps
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Moorland and a lake lie to the west, beside a border county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moor' looks like the noun for heath, but it is the verb to tie up. Leitrim is a county in the Republic of Ireland, on the border with Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Leitrim is one of the thirty-two counties of Ireland.

clue.text: Soused with short hose

indicators.note: the word for hose is cut short of its final letter

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings or tights

explanation.surface: A drunk fellow wearing short stockings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hose' suggests a garden hose; it is legwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is informal for drunk, as is soused.

clue.text: One in fifteen in Society voting in Great Britain approve

definitions.note: a rugby union side has fifteen players

parts.note: PR is proportional representation, a voting system
taken as written
to OK something is to approve it

explanation.surface: One member of a fifteen-strong society votes to approve in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: A Springbok is a player for South Africa's national rugby union team, a side of fifteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Springboks are the South African rugby team, so one is a member of a fifteen.
